info.title: Anyroute API
info.description: Scope: a documented subset of the public HTTP API that the Anyroute router implements. It covers the model catalog, chat completions, embeddings, key creation and listing, generations, status, health and receipts, plus the blind-token issuer keys and purchase (present only when the router enables blind tokens) the Oblivious HTTP gateway keys, gateway and relay list (present only when the router enables Oblivious HTTP) and the Lane: model variants, day-zero candidates and creator royalty claims. Other implemented routes (for example legacy completions, the /v1 aliases, key updates, credits, Stock Token payments, BYOK, teams, wallet sign-in, rankings, provider onboarding and the paymaster) are not described here, and a route's absence from this document does not mean it is absent from the router. Endpoint availability, payment modes and model capabilities are deployment-specific. Errors share the OpenRouter-shaped ApiError body; the 4xx responses each operation can return are declared with the reusable responses in components.responses.

get.summary: List public live models

parameters.name: lane
parameters.description: public (default) lists every live model. attested lists only models with at least one endpoint served under attested retention with a fresh attestation right now. unlinkable lists the same models where the router enables Oblivious HTTP (otherwise 501).

parameters.name: variant
parameters.description: Comma-separated variants to keep: mainstream, native_low_refusal, abliterated. A restricted variant (native_low_refusal, abliterated) is listed only while an attested provider whose attestation reports the in-enclave classifier serves it, and only such endpoints are counted for it.

post.description: Supports standard JSON responses and Server-Sent Events when stream is true. A model must support requested capabilities such as tools or response_format. Auth may use a bearer key, wallet authentication, or the per-call payment flow. A 402 response can contain a quote; follow its payment instructions before retrying the exact request. When the router has x402 enabled, the 402 body is also an x402 v1 payment requirement (x402Version, accepts): sign the exact-scheme USDG authorization and retry with X-PAYMENT; the paid response carries X-PAYMENT-RESPONSE. Two opt-in modes run several billed calls for one request and are off unless the router enables them: model anyroute/council (a panel of models plus a judge; see the council field) and verify "dual" (the same request to two providers; see the verification field). Both are non-streaming only. Where the router enables blind tokens, Authorization: PrivateToken token=<base64url> pays with one token instead of a key (see the Blind tokens tag): the call is charged to a pooled account, the signed receipt carries the token's nullifier and no payer, and the token is spent only if the call is served. A token pays for at most its value, so a request whose worst case costs more is refused with 402 token_value_too_low; council mode and verify are refused with 400 blind_unsupported. A refused, unknown, expired or already spent token is a 401 that carries WWW-Authenticate: PrivateToken challenge="...". Disclosure ceilings and lanes apply to token calls exactly as to key calls. Lane unlinkable, where the router enables Oblivious HTTP, is served only for a request that arrives through the gateway (POST /api/v1/ohttp/gateway) by way of an independent relay, paid with a blind token and never a key, and only by attested providers; otherwise it is refused with 403 (unlinkable_requires_relay, unlinkable_requires_independent_relay, unlinkable_requires_token), 401 with the token challenge when no token is presented, or 409 lane_unavailable when no attested provider serves the model. Streaming is not available through the gateway.

200.description: Completion JSON, or SSE events followed by data: [DONE] when stream is true.

X-PAYMENT-RESPONSE.description: Present when an x402 payment was settled for this call: base64 JSON {success, transaction, network, payer}.

schema.description: SSE data events; event data carries JSON chunks.

post.description: Uses a prepaid API key, or no key with the per-call payment flow (HTTP 402, including x402 when enabled). Input may be a string or a non-empty array with at most 2048 items. Where the router enables blind tokens, Authorization: PrivateToken token=<base64url> pays with one token, exactly as for chat completions.

200.description: Embedding response with usage and signed receipt.

post.summary: Create a root key or authenticated sub-key
post.description: Without Authorization, creates an independent root key with an empty balance. With an authorized management or admin key, creates a virtual sub-key under that account. The response includes the new secret once; store it securely. Root-key creation does not fund the key. Never send a secret in a query string.

201.description: New key metadata and one-time key secret.

get.summary: List keys for the authenticated account

200.description: Key metadata for the authenticated account.

get.summary: List generation summaries
get.description: Returns summaries for the authenticated account. The response's next value can be passed as before to request an older page.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: Opaque cursor returned in next. Pass it through without parsing; current versions may return a legacy ISO-8601 timestamp.

200.description: Generation summaries and the next page cursor, if any.

get.summary: Read one generation record
get.description: Returns a full record only to the account owner, the authenticated paying wallet, or (for a call paid with a blind token, which has no account) whoever presents that spent token in Authorization: PrivateToken. The id is supplied as a query parameter because that is the implemented route; do not put API keys or other credentials in URLs.

get.summary: Read public router configuration
get.description: Returns published runtime configuration, chain public fields, job state and catalog counts, and, where the router runs a Tor onion service, its address as data.onion.address (null otherwise). It is not an uptime guarantee.

get.summary: Check process response
get.description: Returns { ok: true } when this process responds. It does not establish dependency health or uptime.

get.summary: Read a public receipt proof

200.description: Signed receipt and optional anchor proof.

get.summary: The router's receipt signing keys
get.description: Every Ed25519 key the router has signed receipts with, current and retired, as a JWKS. A receipt is checked by canonicalizing its payload (keys sorted, no whitespace), verifying the signature with the key whose kid is the receipt's key_id, and confirming the kid is the first 16 hex characters of SHA-256 of the raw key. The same list is served at /api/v1/receipts/keys.

get.summary: What the router has verified about a provider's attestation
get.description: Public. status is attested only while the router holds a fresh attestation it verified itself, simulated only for development evidence outside production, and unverified otherwise (reason says why). checks lists what was established, each true or false; not_checked lists what this record does not cover. measurement, when present, is the last recorded image, compose and model digests with their transparency-log and on-chain state; attested_now says whether they are what the provider is attested as running now. Nothing here is the provider's own claim repeated back.

get.summary: Proof-time: how long each attesting provider has held a fresh attestation
get.description: Public. For every live or shadow provider that has a TEE and an attestation endpoint: the current status (by the same rule as GET /api/v1/attestation/{providerId}), and the share of the last 24 hours and 7 days in which the router held a fresh attestation it verified itself. A fresh attestation is one the router verified at most fresh_within_ms ago (three attestor intervals) with no failed run since; a failed run, or evidence accepted only as simulated, ends the cover at once. share is the covered part of the time the record spans (observed_ms); when the record does not reach back to the start of the window (history_complete false) the earlier time is unknown and counts neither way, and share is null when nothing is recorded. buckets divides the window into equal slices, each the percent covered, or null before the record begins. Also: measurement changes in the last 7 days, the last measurement change (which fields, from and to), the last failed check as a code with a fixed message (never the provider's own text), the pass rate of the last 7 days' checks, and the latest health-probe and canary outcomes. Nothing here is raw provider output. Returns 501 not_enabled when the router keeps no history (ATTESTATION_HISTORY_DAYS is 0).

501.description: not_enabled: this router keeps no attestation history.

get.summary: A provider's recorded attestation, canary and probe events
get.description: Public. Newest first. Each event is one attestor run (kind attestation: ok or a failure code, the report hash, the TLS pin's SPKI hash when pinned, the verifiers that accepted the quote, the digests the run reported and whether they differ from the previous run's), one canary run (kind canary), or a change of the health probe's outcome (kind probe; only changes are recorded). Events are kept for history_days. Page with before set to the previous page's next: it encodes the moment and id of the last event, so events at the same instant are neither skipped nor repeated. Returns 404 for an unknown provider and 501 not_enabled when the router keeps no history.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: The next value of the previous page.

parameters.name: ok
parameters.description: Only events that passed (true) or failed (false).

501.description: not_enabled: this router keeps no attestation history.

get.summary: The key measurement bundles must be signed with
get.description: Public; 404 until the router is configured with a measurement key. A measurement bundle names the compose hash, source commit and tarball hash, model digest and image digests of a provider's attested software, with an MRTD and RTMR3 allow-list. It counts only if it is signed with this ECDSA P-256 key (SHA-256, DER signature over the bundle's canonical JSON) and the entry recording it in the transparency log verifies. key_id is the SHA-256 of the SubjectPublicKeyInfo.

get.summary: A provider's signed measurement bundles and their transparency-log entries
get.description: Public; 404 until the router is configured with a measurement key. Newest first. Each item carries the bundle, its signature and digest, the status the router reached (pending, verified or rejected, with the reason), the log entry it verified (uuid, index, integration time, whether the inclusion proof, checkpoint signature and signed entry timestamp verified) and, once verified, the log's own copy of the entry (entry_record: body, inclusion proof, signed entry timestamp) so a verifier can check it without asking the log.

post.description: One JSON-RPC 2.0 message per request: initialize, ping, tools/list and tools/call (list_models, chat, get_receipt, verify_receipt), plus notifications, which get an empty 202. Replies are JSON, never a stream; there are no sessions. Only the chat tool needs an API key, which it spends like /api/v1/chat/completions. Malformed JSON or a batch gets HTTP 400, a request carrying a foreign Origin header gets 403 and GET gets 405; all three carry a JSON-RPC error body.

200.description: A JSON-RPC 2.0 response: a result, or an error object with a JSON-RPC code.

202.description: Notification accepted; the body is empty.

get.summary: List the account's saved routes

post.summary: Save a routing policy callable as model @route/<slug>
post.description: Owner or admin. No prompt text is stored.

get.summary: Get a saved route

patch.summary: Update or rename a saved route
patch.description: Each config section sent replaces that section; null clears it.

get.summary: List the account's agent sessions

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: Opaque cursor returned in next. Pass it through without parsing; a plain ISO-8601 timestamp is also accepted.

post.summary: Create a short-lived, budget-capped session key for an agent run
post.description: Owner or admin. The secret is returned once. A session cannot exceed its creator's budget, expiry or model allowlist.

get.summary: A session key's own remaining budget and time
Session detail with recent call metadata (never content)
Spend totals, projection, anomaly flag, series, breakdowns and key budgets
List alert rules and recent firings

post.summary: Create an alert rule (threshold, budget_pct or anomaly)
post.description: Owner or admin. Webhooks must be HTTPS to a public address and are delivered at most 3 times per firing.

get.summary: A provider's disclosure profile and the class it is served under right now
get.description: Public. Every value is what the operator documented, with its own source and date; nothing is inferred from traffic. A provider with no recorded profile returns the conservative defaults (retention logs, jurisdiction unknown, legal hold undeclared, training use unknown, declared false). current.class is attested only when retention is declared attested and the provider's TEE attestation is fresh now; current.simulated is true when that attestation is a development report (never accepted in production).

put.summary: Replace a provider's disclosure profile (operator only)
put.description: Requires the operator token in X-Admin-Token or as a bearer token; an API key is not accepted. The profile is replaced as a whole: a claim that is left out reverts to its conservative default. A retention other than logs needs a legal_hold claim, and retention attested needs a provider with a TEE and attestation endpoint.

409.description: provider_not_attestable: retention attested was claimed for a provider with no TEE or attestation endpoint (or a development TEE in production).

put.summary: Declare a model's variant, license and weights provenance (operator only)
put.description: Requires the operator token in X-Admin-Token or as a bearer token; an API key is not accepted. The record is replaced as a whole. The model need not be listed by any provider yet: classify it first. native_low_refusal and abliterated are restricted variants and need license and base_model on record. status candidate routes the model to no provider until the record is written again as servable.

get.summary: Day-zero candidates and their latest scores (operator only)
get.description: Requires the operator token. When enabled, the router watches Hugging Face for new fine-tunes of the base models it is configured with, keeps those whose model card carries an allowed license (MIT or Apache-2.0 by default) and records why it rejected the rest. Status: discovered, rejected, evaluated, failed, approved or servable.

get.summary: One day-zero candidate (operator only)

put.summary: Say which provider offer serves a candidate's weights (operator only)
put.description: The offer's model must declare the candidate's Hugging Face repository as its hugging_face_id, so an evaluation of one set of weights cannot approve a different model. From the moment a repository is a candidate, a model that declares it is routed to no provider until the candidate is servable.

409.description: repo_mismatch: the offer's model does not declare the candidate's repository. candidate_rejected: the candidate was rejected. invalid_state: the candidate is already approved.

post.summary: Run the probe sets against a candidate's endpoint (operator only)
post.description: Sends the endpoint 16 benign prompts that base models commonly over-refuse (fiction, security education, medical and legal information; none harmful or illegal), 12 capability prompts with exact checks (arithmetic, JSON format, instruction following) and the router's canary set. The scores are stored. The candidate passes when its refusal rate is at most DAYZERO_MAX_REFUSAL_RATE, its capability score at least DAYZERO_MIN_CAPABILITY, its canary accuracy at least DAYZERO_MIN_CANARY and the canary precision check does not contradict the declared quantization. An approved or servable candidate that fails loses its approval and stops being served.

409.description: no_endpoint: link an endpoint first. endpoint_unavailable: the linked offer or provider is not live. candidate_rejected: the candidate was rejected.
invalid_state: only an evaluated candidate can be approved.

post.summary: Make an approved candidate servable (operator only)
post.description: Succeeds only if the linked provider is served under attested retention with a fresh attestation and its attestation reports the in-enclave classifier as enabled: the same test routing applies to a request. Otherwise 409 not_servable says why and nothing changes. The router repeats this for approved candidates on every day-zero run.

409.description: invalid_state: only an approved candidate can be promoted. not_servable: no attested provider that reports the classifier serves it now; error.metadata.candidate is the candidate.

post.summary: Get a challenge to claim a model's creator royalty
post.description: Public and rate limited. The model must have a Hugging Face weights source on record. Commit file_content to the file named in file, on the main branch of hugging_face_id, then call the verify endpoint before expires_at. The address is the one that will receive the royalty.

hf_handle.description: Optional: refused if it is not the owner of the weights source.

409.description: not_claimable: the model has no Hugging Face weights source on record.

get.summary: Read a creator claim

post.summary: Check the published challenge and record the royalty recipient
post.description: Public and rate limited. The router reads the repository's owner and the claim file through the Hugging Face API. The owner must still be the handle the challenge was issued to and the file must contain the challenge on its own line. On success the address becomes the model's royalty recipient at the router's default rate (5 percent unless configured otherwise, at most 20 percent): it is registered in the royalty contract first when one is configured, then recorded, and every later call to the model includes the royalty in its price. Verifying a verified claim returns it again.

409.description: claim_stale: the model's weights source changed since the challenge was issued.

410.description: claim_expired: the challenge is no longer valid; start a new claim.

502.description: chain_failed: the royalty contract registration failed and nothing was recorded; verify again. hf_unavailable: Hugging Face could not be read.

get.summary: Issuer keys, the token challenge and token prices
get.description: Public; 404 unless the router enables blind tokens. One 2048-bit RSA issuer key per denomination (1000, 10000 and 100000 token-units) per epoch (a week), published before the epoch starts. token_key_id is the SHA-256 of the key's RFC 9578 SubjectPublicKeyInfo (token_key, base64url), so a client can check the key against its id. A key issues only while its status is issuing; its tokens stay redeemable until redeem_until. Every token must carry challenge_digest, the SHA-256 of the published challenge. commitments are the per-epoch values a BlindIssuer contract records. Nothing in this response is signed: compare commitments with a value recorded independently (for example on chain) before trusting the keys.

post.description: Debits the key's credits through the ledger and returns one blind signature per blinded message, in order. The client blinds the token inputs (RFC 9474) with the key named by token_key_id, and unblinds the signatures locally; the router stores counts only, never the blinded messages, the signatures or the tokens. Sending the same request again after a lost response returns the same signatures without charging again (replayed: true). Purchases count against the key's budget and are rate limited per key, capped per request (max_batch) and per account per day. A key restricted to some models cannot buy tokens. 404 unless the router enables blind tokens.

409.description: The key's epoch is not open yet (epoch_not_open), has ended (epoch_closed) or was revoked (token_key_revoked), or the same purchase is still being processed (purchase_in_progress).

get.summary: Gateway key configuration (RFC 9458 section 3)
get.description: Public; 404 unless the router enables Oblivious HTTP. One key configuration in application/ohttp-keys form: key identifier, KEM (DHKEM X25519 HKDF-SHA256), public key, and the KDF and AEAD pairs offered (HKDF-SHA256 with AES-128-GCM). The key changes every epoch (a day by default) and keeps opening requests for a grace period after that. This response is not signed: check it against the signed key list (GET /api/v1/ohttp/key-list) before use. Also served at /.well-known/ohttp-gateway.

503.description: The gateway has no usable key right now (ohttp_no_key). Retry after Retry-After.

post.summary: Oblivious HTTP gateway: unwrap an encapsulated request, serve it, wrap the response
post.description: Sent by a relay (or, without the privacy benefit, directly). The body is a message/ohttp-req: a binary HTTP request (RFC 9292) sealed to the gateway key. The gateway serves it on the router's own routes and answers 200 with a message/ohttp-res that carries the whole inner response, errors included, so an inner 4xx is inside the encapsulation. Reachable routes: POST chat/completions and completions (non-streaming only), POST embeddings, POST blind/purchase, GET blind/keys, GET models; anything else is an inner 404 route_not_allowed. Of the request's headers only Authorization, Content-Type, Accept, X-Anyroute-Lane and X-Anyroute-Disclosure-Max are passed on. Responses are zero-padded to a multiple of 256 bytes. A relay identifies itself with Authorization: Bearer <key_id>:<secret>; a request without it is treated as direct and is not served the unlinkable lane. Errors before the request could be unwrapped are plain HTTP: 415, 413, 400, 422 (unknown key identifier or a request that does not decrypt, application/problem+json), 401 (a relay credential that is not recognised) and 429. Do not retry a failed encapsulated request automatically; a repeated ciphertext is answered with an inner 409 replayed_request.

413.description: The encapsulated request is larger than the gateway accepts.

415.description: The content type is not message/ohttp-req.

422.description: The key identifier is unknown, expired or revoked, the ciphersuite is not offered, or the request does not decrypt with the key it names. Fetch the key configuration again.

get.summary: Gateway key history, signed and hash-chained
get.description: Public; 404 unless the router enables Oblivious HTTP. Every gateway key with its configuration, acceptance window and status, the next epoch's key listed as upcoming before it is served, and the relay list. The document is signed with the router's receipt signing key (Ed25519 over the canonical JSON of data; keys at GET /api/v1/receipts/keys, also registered on chain), and each key's entry_hash chains to the one before it, so a client can pin log.head and notice a key that was removed or replaced. A key's private half is destroyed when its window ends (private_key_destroyed).

get.summary: Relays clients may use for the unlinkable lane
get.description: Public; 404 unless the router enables Oblivious HTTP. Each relay has its operator, its URL and a key_id (an identifier of the credential the relay presents to the gateway, published so it is on record; the router does not verify it beyond authenticating the relay). independent is false for a relay run by the gateway's own operator: the unlinkable lane is not served through it. Pick a relay whose operator is not the gateway operator.

get.summary: $ANYR balance, tier, perks, tier ladder and free credits for the wallet behind this key
get.description: Only keys from wallet sign-in have a wallet; any other key gets the same shape with wallet null and a hint. Tiers apply only when the router sets both ANYR_TOKEN_ADDRESS and HOLDER_TIERS (enabled). The balance is read live (cached for 5 minutes); when it cannot be read, balance_error is true and no tier applies. discount_bps lowers Anyroute's own fee rates (the per-call margin and the BYOK fee), never below 0; prepaid calls carry no margin, so for them the discount is 0.

patch.summary: Update an alert rule (kind cannot change; webhook_url null removes it)

BearerAuth.description: Send the key in Authorization. Never put it in a URL.

WalletAuth.name: X-Wallet-Auth
WalletAuth.description: Wallet authentication header for supported per-call flows.

PrivateToken.name: Authorization
PrivateToken.description: Only where the router enables blind tokens. `PrivateToken token=<base64url>`: one Privacy Pass token (RFC 9578 type 0x0002, 354 bytes) bought with POST /api/v1/blind/purchase. Each token can be spent once.

Payment.name: X-Payment
Payment.description: Payment for this exact request: a CallPay transaction hash, or an x402 payment (base64 JSON {x402Version, scheme, network, payload}) from a 402 quote. Do not replay blindly.

PayWith.name: X-Pay-With
PayWith.description: Configured Stock Token symbol for a key with an active session.

DisclosureMax.name: X-Anyroute-Disclosure-Max
DisclosureMax.description: Same as provider.disclosure. When both are given the stricter one applies.

Lane.name: X-Anyroute-Lane
Lane.description: Same as provider.lane. When both are given the stricter one applies. unlinkable is served only where the router enables Oblivious HTTP (otherwise 501), and then only through a relay with a blind token.

Disclosure.description: The disclosure class the answering provider was served under: attested (retention declared attested and a fresh TEE attestation), policy (a documented no-retention policy, no legal hold) or vendor-forwarded (anything else). On a stream it is sent only when every provider the request can reach shares one class; the signed receipt always carries it.

LaneServed.description: The lane the request asked for.

ApiError.description: OpenRouter-shaped API error. A 402 payment response may include payment metadata and is not a signal to repeat payment automatically.

BadRequest.description: The request body, JSON or parameters failed validation. error.type is, for example, invalid_request, invalid_json or invalid_guardrails; do not retry the same request unchanged.

Unauthorized.description: Authentication is missing or was rejected: no API key, an unknown, disabled or expired key, or invalid wallet authentication. error.type is missing_key, invalid_key, key_disabled, key_expired or invalid_wallet_auth.

PaymentRequired.description: The call cannot be paid: the balance or the key's budget is insufficient (insufficient_credits, key_budget_exceeded), or a per-call payment is required or was not accepted (payment_required, payment_pending, payment_insufficient, payment_unknown_quote, payment_failed). A payment_required quote is in error.metadata and binds to this exact request; never repeat a payment automatically.

X-Payment-Required.description: Present on a per-call payment quote; names the payment asset.

WWW-Authenticate.description: Present on a per-call payment quote; carries the chain and quote nonce.

Forbidden.description: The key is valid but may not do this: its role does not allow the action, or its model allowlist excludes the model. error.type is forbidden or model_not_allowed.

NotFound.description: The model, provider route, key, team, generation or receipt does not exist or is not visible to the caller. error.type is, for example, not_found, model_not_found or no_providers.

DisclosureUnavailable.description: 409. No provider meets provider.disclosure or provider.lane, though the model has providers that would otherwise serve the request. error.type is disclosure_unavailable or lane_unavailable. On chat completions it can also be verification_unavailable: verify "dual" found fewer than two providers of the model that support temperature and seed (on lane attested: fewer than two different attested providers of the model). A council with an attested seat (a member or the judge) that has no attested provider is refused with lane_unavailable, and error.metadata.council_seat names the seat. The request is never routed to a provider that does not meet the setting; nothing was sent to any provider and nothing was charged.

LaneNotAvailable.description: 501 lane_not_available. Lane unlinkable is not available on this router: it needs the Oblivious HTTP gateway and blind tokens, which it does not run. Nothing was sent to any provider.

DisclosureProviderDown.description: 503 disclosure_provider_unavailable. Providers that meet provider.disclosure or provider.lane exist but are all in an outage right now. Retry after Retry-After; the request is not routed to any other provider and nothing was charged.

TooManyRequests.description: A rate limit was reached (rate_limited). Wait for the Retry-After interval before retrying.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before retrying, when the limit reports it.

pricing.description: Prices are returned as decimal strings per token; consult the live response.

disclosure.description: How many live endpoints are served under each disclosure class right now.

creator.description: Address that receives the model's creator royalty, once claimed.

royalty_bps.description: Creator royalty in basis points of the notional price; 0 until a creator is recorded.

variant.description: native_low_refusal and abliterated are restricted: they are routed only to providers served under attested retention with a fresh attestation whose attestation reported the in-enclave hard-block classifier as enabled. Whatever lane or disclosure setting a request carries, and however the provider is pinned, they are never sent to a public or vendor-forwarded provider.

variant_source.description: declared: an operator recorded the variant. candidate: the model is the weights of a day-zero candidate. inferred: nobody has classified the model and its name says its refusals were removed, so it is treated as abliterated. default: no record, treated as mainstream.

license.description: License identifier from the weights' model card, when an operator recorded one.

base_model.description: The model these weights derive from.

weights.description: Where the weights came from, as recorded by the operator.

revision.description: Commit the weights were taken from.

digest.description: sha256:<hex> of the weights, when recorded (for a day-zero model, the model digest in the provider's verified attestation).

creator_handle.description: Hugging Face handle of the uploader.

model.description: Public model ID, optionally with a supported routing modifier. The reserved ID anyroute/council selects council mode when the router enables it.

tools.description: Requires a model/provider that supports tools.

response_format.description: Requires a model/provider that supports the requested response format.

verify.description: Send the same request to two providers of the model at temperature 0 with a fixed seed and compare the outputs. Both calls are billed. Needs the router's council feature; not combinable with stream, models, cache or n above 1. Provider preferences, disclosure ceiling and lane apply to both calls. With lane attested the two calls go to two different attested providers of the model (retention declared attested, attestation fresh); each receipt then records its provider's attestation as payload.attestation_ref, and the verification field carries attested and attestation_refs next to agree. If two such providers do not exist the answer is 409, and nothing is sent or charged.

CouncilRequest.description: Used with model anyroute/council. Members are called in parallel through the normal routing path, then the judge chooses one answer (judge) or writes a final one (fuse). Every call is billed and receipted; the worst case of all calls is held up front. provider preferences, including a disclosure ceiling or lane, apply to every member and to the judge.

models.description: Member model IDs. Falls back to the router's configured default when omitted.

judge.description: Model ID of the judge. Falls back to the router's configured default when omitted.

mode.description: judge returns one member's answer unchanged; fuse returns the judge's own text and does not support tools or response_format.

max_cost_usd.description: Refuse the request with 402 council_budget_exceeded unless the worst case of every call fits. Lower max_tokens to fit.

min_members.description: Members that must answer before the judge runs. Defaults to 2.

attested.description: true holds every member and the judge to the attested lane (retention declared attested and a fresh attestation the router verified), the same as provider.lane attested for the whole council. Nothing is downgraded or dropped: a member, or the judge, with no attested provider refuses the request with 409 lane_unavailable (503 while attested providers are down), and nothing is sent or charged. The response then carries attested and attestation_refs in council, and each call's receipt carries attestation_ref. A production router has few attested providers today, so this often returns that 409.

CouncilResult.description: Present on council responses. The top-level receipt is the judge's call and its signed payload carries the same members list; its disclosure is the weakest class among all the calls.

disclosure.description: The class this member was served under.

receipt_id.description: Null for a member that failed; it was not billed.

total_cost.description: USD charged across every member and the judge.

attested.description: Present when the council ran on the attested lane (council.attested true, or lane attested). True only when every member and the judge were served under the attested class and each has a reference in attestation_refs. Signed in the top-level receipt.

attestation_simulated.description: True when any attestation behind the council is a development report; a production router never accepts one.

attestation_refs.description: One entry per call that took part, members in order and then the judge: what the router itself verified about the provider that served it. Signed in the top-level receipt.

label.description: The member's label; absent for the judge.

AttestationRef.description: The attestation the router had verified for a provider when it served a call: the hash of the attestation report and, when the provider attested through a self-signed TLS certificate, the pinned key the router's connection to it accepts. Recorded in the signed receipt of a call made under an attested council or attested dual verification, as payload.attestation_ref. Receipts made any other way do not carry it. The same data is at GET /api/v1/attestation/{providerId}.

tee.description: tdx, snp, nvidia-cc, tinfoil or dev.

report_hash.description: Hash of the attestation report the router verified (the payload.attestation field of the same receipt).

tls_pin.description: Null when the provider did not attest through a self-signed certificate.

spki_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the pinned certificate's SubjectPublicKeyInfo.

attestation_ref.description: SHA-256 of the quote the certificate names.

simulated.description: true when the report is development evidence.

VerificationResult.description: Present on verify "dual" responses. agree is true when both providers returned the same output (exactly, or after whitespace is collapsed); it says nothing about whether either provider is attested, unless the request used lane attested (then attested and attestation_refs say so). The response body is the first provider's output.

attested.description: Present only on lane attested. True when both calls were served by two different providers under the attested class and each has a reference in attestation_refs. Signed in both receipts, next to agree.

attestation_refs.description: One entry per call that ran (label A or B), in the same order as receipts. Each receipt also carries its own provider's reference as payload.attestation_ref.

ProviderPreferences.description: Provider routing preferences (order, only, ignore, sort, max_price, private and others) plus the disclosure options below.

disclosure.description: Ceiling on how a prompt may be handled. none: only providers whose retention is declared attested and whose TEE attestation is fresh. policy: those, plus providers with a documented no-retention policy and no legal hold. any: no filter. Never silently relaxed: if nothing qualifies the request fails (409, or 503 when qualifying providers are down). A request with a ceiling never uses the response cache.

lane.description: public: no additional filter. attested: same as disclosure none. unlinkable: attested providers only, and only for a request that arrived through the Oblivious HTTP gateway by way of an independent relay and is paid with a blind token (see Oblivious HTTP); 501 where the router does not enable Oblivious HTTP, 403 unlinkable_requires_relay, unlinkable_requires_independent_relay or unlinkable_requires_token otherwise.

source.description: The document or statement the value comes from.

as_of.description: The date the source was checked.

declared.description: False when the operator has recorded nothing; every value is then the conservative default.

retention.description: attested: the provider states prompts are not retained and runs in a TEE. policy: a documented no-retention policy. logs: prompts may be logged (default).

jurisdiction.description: Where the operator is subject to legal process; unknown by default.

active.description: null = not declared. A no-retention policy is not trusted while a hold is active or undeclared.

claims.description: The source and date behind each value; null when the value is a default.

simulated.description: True when the attestation behind an attested class is a development report.

DisclosureInput.description: Every claim is optional and carries its own source and date.

management.description: Only honored for authorized authenticated sub-key creation; root-key management is never granted by this field.

kid.description: First 16 hex characters of SHA-256 of the raw key.

fresh_within_ms.description: How old a verified attestation may be and still count as fresh.

attested.description: Runs that passed with hardware evidence (simulated evidence is not counted).

share.description: Covered part of the time the record spans within the window; null when nothing is recorded.

observed_ms.description: How much of the window the record spans.

history_complete.description: False when the record does not reach back to the start of the window; the earlier time is unknown, not covered and not uncovered.

buckets.description: Equal slices from the start of the window to now (48 for 24h, 84 for 7d): percent covered, or null before the record begins.

share.description: Covered part of the time the record spans within the window; null when nothing is recorded.

observed_ms.description: How much of the window the record spans.

history_complete.description: False when the record does not reach back to the start of the window; the earlier time is unknown, not covered and not uncovered.

buckets.description: Equal slices from the start of the window to now (48 for 24h, 84 for 7d): percent covered, or null before the record begins.

digests.description: Digests only: image_digest, compose_hash, model_digest, mrtd, rtmr0 to rtmr3, measurement.

from.description: Digests only: image_digest, compose_hash, model_digest, mrtd, rtmr0 to rtmr3, measurement.

to.description: Digests only: image_digest, compose_hash, model_digest, mrtd, rtmr0 to rtmr3, measurement.

probe.description: The latest health-probe outcome and when it began.

reason.description: A code from a fixed list with its message; never the provider's own text.
A code from a fixed list with its message; never the provider's own text.
A code from a fixed list with its message; never the provider's own text.

simulated.description: Development evidence: never counted as a fresh attestation.

tls_spki_sha256.description: SPKI hash of the certificate the connection was pinned to, when it was.

measurements.description: Digests only: image_digest, compose_hash, model_digest, mrtd, rtmr0 to rtmr3, measurement.

measurement_changed.description: The run's digests differ from the previous accepted run's, comparing the fields both report.

next.description: Pass as before for the next page; null on the last page.

verifiers.description: The verifiers that accepted the quote; empty unless status is attested.

measurement.description: Last recorded digests (image_digest, compose_hash, model_digest), status, attested_now, registers { mrtd, rtmr3 } of the recorded quote, transparency_log { found, inclusion_verified, checkpoint_signature_verified, subject (measurement_bundle or image_digest), entry_url, bundle, ... } and registry { address, state, tx_hash, registered_at }.

payload.description: Signed fields. Among them, disclosure (attested, policy or vendor-forwarded) and lane (public, attested or unlinkable) record how the call was served; attestation_simulated is true when the attestation behind an attested call is a development report. attestation_ref (see AttestationRef) is present on calls made under an attested council or attested dual verification. For a call paid with a blind token, payer is null and nullifier (the SHA-256 of the spent token) and token_key_id are present; nothing names an account. Receipts issued before these fields existed do not carry them.

models.description: Catalog model ids in fallback order; no nested @route/.

provider.description: Provider preferences: order, only, ignore, allow_fallbacks, sort (price|latency|throughput), data_collection, zdr, require_parameters, max_price.

params.description: Default request parameters from a closed whitelist (temperature, top_p, top_k, min_p, top_a, frequency_penalty, presence_penalty, repetition_penalty, max_tokens, seed, stop, reasoning, verbosity). Prompt fields are rejected.

model.description: Use as the request model, e.g. @route/my-coder.

allowed_models.description: Catalog ids or @route/<slug>; must be within the creator's allowlist.

metadata.description: Labels only, at most 2 KB; prompt-like keys are refused.

SpendReport.description: Spend for the caller's scope (a management key sees its account; other keys see themselves). UTC calendar.

min.description: Minimum balance in whole tokens (decimal string).

rpm_multiplier.description: Multiplies the key's rpm and tpm limits.

discount_bps.description: Lowers Anyroute's own fee rates by this many basis points, never below 0.

challenge_digest.description: SHA-256 of the challenge, hex; the challenge_digest field of every token.

unit_price_usd.description: USD per token-unit for keys created from now on; each key states its own value_usd.

commitment.description: keccak256(abi.encode(uint64 epoch, uint32[] denominations, bytes32[] keyIds)), as recorded by BlindIssuer.commitEpoch.

value_usd.description: What one token of this key is worth; fixed for the key's life.

issued.description: Tokens signed with this key (a count).

keys.description: Oldest first; at most the latest 512.

key_id.description: The 8-bit key identifier: the epoch modulo 256.

entry_hash.description: SHA-256 chain: this entry committed to the one before it.

first_prev.description: The entry hash before the first key listed (64 zeros when the list starts at the first key ever).

key_id.description: A receipt signing key; see GET /api/v1/receipts/keys.

sig.description: Base64 Ed25519 signature over the canonical JSON of data.

key_id.description: Identifier of the credential this relay presents to the gateway.

independent.description: False when the relay's operator is the gateway's own operator.

token_key_id.description: A key whose status is issuing.

items.description: 256 bytes, base64url: the blinded token input, below the key's modulus.

blinded_msgs.description: Distinct blinded messages, at most max_batch.

replayed.description: True when this exact purchase had already been made; nothing was charged again.

signatures.description: signatures[i] answers blinded_msgs[i]; 256 bytes each, base64url.

enabled.description: Whether holder tiers apply to requests on this router.

wallet.description: The wallet behind this key (wallet sign-in keys only).

balance.description: Token balance in whole tokens (decimal string).

balance_error.description: True when the balance could not be read; no tier applies until it can.

rpm.description: This key's request limit per minute with the multiplier (0 = unlimited).

credits_received.description: Free inference credits paid to this wallet, newest first. They pay for inference only and are not withdrawable.

ModelLaneInput.description: A model's lane record. native_low_refusal and abliterated need license and base_model.

status.description: candidate routes the model to no provider.

source.description: For example huggingface:owner/repo. A creator claim is checked against this repository.

creator_handle.description: Hugging Face handle of the uploader.

revision.description: The revision seen at discovery; the one evaluated.

reason.description: Why a candidate was rejected or failed.

model.description: The catalog model that serves it, once linked.

refusal_rate.description: Share of the benign probe prompts the endpoint refused.

capability_score.description: Share of the exact-check prompts answered correctly.

handle.description: Owner of the repository, from its id.

file.description: File name to commit to the main branch of the repository.

file_content.description: What the file must contain: the challenge on its own line.

webhook_url.description: HTTPS, public address only; stored encrypted.
